$comment: Spec-by-example for .clx. Run: node lab/clx-lang/parse.test.cjs. Every implementation (JS prototype, Rust port) must produce exactly these bindings/variants and these diagnostics (level@line exact, message by prefix). `why` records the decision the case pins down; see lab/clx-lang/#corpus.

cases.name: hold: clx alias expands to either trigger
cases.why: clx is sugar for (space|capslock); alternation yields one variant per trigger, space first.

cases.name: hold: commutative group is order-insensitive
cases.why: (capslock+space) and (space+capslock) normalize to the same pattern, so they collide as duplicates; the variants keep the written order.

diags: warn@2: duplicate pattern, earlier binding on line 1 wins

cases.name: tap: group tap
cases.why: A tapped group is down-in-order, up-in-reverse. Single letters are letters (no s/c trigger aliases).

cases.name: tap: bare key at top level is a tap
cases.why: h and h. are the same pattern; both warn because there is no hold and no trigger.
cases.src:
h => k left
a. => k b

diags: warn@1: pattern has no hold and no trigger — this would fire on plain typing
warn@2: pattern has no hold and no trigger — this would fire on plain typing

cases.name: nesting: inner hold inside outer
cases.why: Inner pressed after outer, released before it.

cases.name: nesting: modifier decorates body
cases.why: shift[ 3 ] inside clx is how Space+Shift+3 (move window) is written.

cases.name: body: multi-key body is a sequence
cases.why: Each body key fires on its own key-down, in order.

cases.name: body: explicit tap inside body equals bare key
cases.why: a. and a are the same inside a body (normalize drops the dot at depth>0).

cases.name: body: bare group inside body is an error
cases.why: A group must say [ or . — a bare group is ambiguous (Q: keep; single keys default to tap, groups do not).

diags: error@1: a group must be followed by "[" (hold) or "." (tap)

cases.name: unclosed hold: legal, warned, fires on key-down
cases.why: Locked mode has this shape. Variant has no closing edge.

diags: warn@1: hold is never closed — legal (fires on key-down, like locked mode) but check for a missing "]"

cases.name: unclosed hold: nested
cases.why: The outer hold is what is unclosed; the inner one closed normally.

diags: warn@1: hold is never closed — legal (fires on key-down, like locked mode) but check for a missing "]"

cases.name: empty hold body warns
cases.why: clx[ ] would be a trigger tap wearing hold syntax; the tap form is clx. (decided 2026-09-15).

diags: warn@1: empty hold body — a tap is written with "." (e.g. clx.)

cases.name: hold on a plain key is a tap-hold (Q3): warned
cases.why: f[ j ] needs the engine to defer f until it knows whether j follows (home-row-mod territory); a modifier hold (alt[ 1 ]) is a plain global hotkey and a trigger hold is the normal case. Decided 2026-09-15: parser warns, engine v1 loader rejects plain-key holds.
cases.src:
f[ j ] => k left
alt[ 1 ] => desktop 1
(a+b)[ c ] => k d

diags: warn@1: hold on a plain key is a tap-hold ("f" must be buffered until the body arrives) — not supported by the engine (Q3)
warn@3: hold on a plain key is a tap-hold ("a+b" must be buffered until the body arrives) — not supported by the engine (Q3)

cases.name: duplicate pattern: first wins
cases.why: Matches the engine's first-module-wins dispatch; later line warns.
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => k left
clx[ h ] => k right

diags: warn@2: duplicate pattern, earlier binding on line 1 wins

cases.name: punctuation keys: bare and named
cases.why: Q2: - and = accepted bare because F11/F12 use them; minus/equal are the canonical names so bare and named collide as duplicates.
cases.src:
clx[ - ] => k f11
clx[ = ] => k f12
clx[ minus ] => k f11

diags: warn@3: duplicate pattern, earlier binding on line 1 wins

cases.name: pointer keys parse but warn
cases.why: No mouse hook in the engine yet (WH_MOUSE_LL / CGEventTap mouse mask).
cases.src:
clx[ wheeldown ] => scroll down
mb4[ h ] => k left

diags: warn@1: pointer key "wheeldown" in a pattern: parses, but the engine has no mouse hook yet (WH_MOUSE_LL / CGEventTap mouse mask)
warn@2: pointer key "mb4" in a pattern: parses, but the engine has no mouse hook yet (WH_MOUSE_LL / CGEventTap mouse mask)

cases.name: ordered group: bare group at top level is an error
cases.why: Same rule as inside a body: (a->b) alone does not say hold or tap.

diags: error@1: a group must be followed by "[" (hold) or "." (tap)

cases.name: mixed connectors in one group is an error
cases.why: Nest instead: (a+b)|c is not expressible in one group.

diags: warn@1: hold on a plain key is a tap-hold ("a+b+c" must be buffered until the body arrives) — not supported by the engine (Q3)
error@1: mixed connectors in one group: "+" and "|" — use nested groups

cases.name: top-level sequence parses (rejected by the engine, Q4)
cases.why: Juxtaposition is a sequence; no double-tap feature (lab/double-tap), so the Rust loader rejects multi-gesture patterns. The parser still produces the cross product of variants.
cases.src: clx[ h ] clx[ h ] => k left

cases.name: alternation of three triggers
cases.why: Variants follow the written order of the alternatives.

cases.name: nested alternation is a cross product
cases.why: Outer × inner alternatives, outer-major order.

diags: warn@1: hold on a plain key is a tap-hold ("a+b" must be buffered until the body arrives) — not supported by the engine (Q3)

cases.name: lexical: case-insensitive, tabs, CRLF, trailing comment
cases.why: Key names fold to lower case; whitespace is free; CRLF files parse; # comments anywhere.
cases.src:
CLX[	H	]	=>	k left # cursor

# comment line
clx[ 2 ] => k f2

cases.name: lexical: no spaces needed
cases.why: clx[h]=>k left is one binding.

cases.name: action: k key with modifiers
cases.why: c s w a prefixes, order preserved.
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => k c-s-a
clx[ j ] => k w-p
clx[ k ] => k ctrl

cases.name: action: k bare - and = are minus and equal
cases.why: Same as the pattern side (Q2); previously lexed as a broken modifier prefix.
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => k -
clx[ j ] => k =

cases.name: action: k string with escapes
cases.why: \n \t \" \\ escapes, verbatim from the agent language.

cases.name: action: block with waits
cases.why: ; separates; trailing and doubled ; are tolerated; newlines inside a block are fine.
cases.src: clx[ g ] => { k "hi"; w 200ms;; k enter; }

cases.name: action: empty block warns
cases.why: Decided 2026-09-15: { } is almost certainly a mistake.

diags: warn@1: empty action block — the binding does nothing

cases.name: action: built-ins are free-form (Q5)
cases.why: Unknown names are for the engine to reject at load time, not the parser.
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => frobnicate 1 two "three"
clx[ v ] => voice

cases.name: action: ; outside a block is an error
cases.why: Sequences need braces; the line is dropped.
cases.src: clx[ h ] => k left ; k right

diags: error@1: unexpected ";" after binding

cases.name: action: missing action is an error
cases.why: The binding is dropped, not kept with an empty block.

diags: error@1: expected an action after "=>", found end of file

cases.name: action: missing => is an error

diags: error@1: expected "=>" but found end of file

cases.name: action: leading => is an error, not a crash
cases.why: Regression: an empty pattern at file start used to throw in span calculation.

diags: error@1: expected a gesture pattern

cases.name: action: bad k / w arguments are errors, line dropped
cases.why: k takes one key or one string; w takes 200ms or 3s (no decimals).
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => k c-
clx[ j ] => w 2
clx[ k ] => w 1.5s
clx[ l ] => k é

diags: error@1: k takes one key (k a, k c-c) or one string (k "text")
error@2: w takes a duration like 200ms or 3s
error@3: w takes a duration like 200ms or 3s
error@4: k takes one key (k a, k c-c) or one string (k "text")
error@4: unexpected character "é"

cases.name: action: agent-only verbs are not part of .clx
cases.why: scan / S / ? are runtime verbs of clx agent, not bindings; they do not parse here (decided 2026-09-15).
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => scan ID 0 0 10 10 dark>3 { k up }
clx[ j ] => ? screen

diags: error@1: unexpected character ">"
error@2: expected an action after "=>"
error@2: unexpected character "?"

cases.name: pointer: m legacy forms
cases.why: m x y, m x y c, m 50% 50%, m cur, m cur +dx +dy, m @mark, hover is m.
cases.src:
clx[ a ] => m 400 300 c
clx[ b ] => m 50% 50%
clx[ c ] => m cur
clx[ d ] => m cur +300 0
clx[ e ] => { mark here; m @here }
clx[ f ] => hover @"OK"

cases.name: pointer: click forms
cases.why: [mods-]button [target] [xN]; default left, x1 = once; dbl is click x2; buttons l r m x1 x2.
cases.src:
clx[ a ] => click
clx[ b ] => click r @"OK"
clx[ c ] => click s-l 50% 50% x3
clx[ d ] => dbl @"Untitled.txt"
clx[ e ] => click x2
clx[ f ] => click c-a-r cur +10 -10

cases.name: pointer: drag, md/mu, scroll, wf
cases.why: drag from -> to [button]; md/mu default left; scroll dir [n|px] [target]; wf takes a string (legacy) or an element target.
cases.src:
clx[ a ] => drag win 50% 90% -> win 50% 10%
clx[ b ] => drag 10 10 -> 20 20 r
clx[ c ] => { md; m cur +300 0; mu }
clx[ d ] => scroll up 240px @"Sidebar"
clx[ e ] => scroll left 2 cur
clx[ f ] => wf "Save" 3s
clx[ g ] => wf @button:"Save" 3s

bindings: 3: (capslock|space)[ c ] => { md left; m cursor +300 +0; mu left }

cases.name: pointer: absolute coordinates may be negative (Q9)
cases.why: Absolute px are virtual-desktop coordinates, which are negative left of / above the primary display.

cases.name: pointer: mixing px and % in one target is an error

diags: error@1: mix of px and % in one target

cases.name: pointer: bad click count / scroll direction are errors
cases.why: x0 is not a target or a count; scroll needs up/down/left/right.
cases.src:
clx[ h ] => click x0
clx[ j ] => scroll sideways

diags: error@1: not a target: "x0"
error@2: scroll needs a direction: up down left right

cases.name: pointer: screen-relative target is not supported yet
cases.why: Draft only; today it fails to parse. When added it should be `screen N x y`.

diags: error@1: m needs a target: x y, N% N%, win/cur/screen x y, @"text", or @mark
error@1: screen-relative targets ("screen N x y") are not supported yet

cases.name: keys: unknown key name is an error

diags: error@1: unknown key "foo"

cases.name: keys: stray ] and [ are errors
cases.src:
clx[ h ] ] => k a
clx[ [ h ] => k a

diags: error@1: expected "=>" but found "]"
error@2: expected "]" to close the hold
error@2: expected "=>" but found "["

cases.name: keys: digit 0 and ctrl as a held modifier
cases.src:
clx[ 0 ] => desktop 10
clx[ ctrl[ h ] ] => k home

cases.name: keys: a hold after ] is an error (no double-tap operator)
cases.why: clx[ v ]. is not a thing; there is no tap-after-hold form.

diags: error@1: expected "=>" but found "."

cases.name: empty file and comment-only file
